name: Kṛṣṇa
summary: In Bhagavad Gītā 1–3: Arjuna's charioteer, who blows the conch Pāñcajanya (1.15), stations the chariot between the armies (1.24–25) and, from 2.2, teaches Arjuna ('śrī bhagavān uvāca'): the imperishable embodied self, svadharma, buddhi-yoga and action without claim on fruits, the person of steady wisdom, sacrifice and loka-saṃgraha, and desire as the enemy. He calls himself the original declarer of the twofold commitment (3.3), says he acts though he has nothing to gain (3.22–24), and asks Arjuna to resign all actions to him (3.30).

name: Arjuna
summary: In Bhagavad Gītā 1–3: the Pāṇḍava warrior (conch Devadatta, bow Gāṇḍīva) who, seeing his kin in both armies, is overcome by pity and grief, argues against fighting (1.28–46, 2.4–8), declares himself Kṛṣṇa's disciple and asks for instruction (2.7), says 'I will not fight' (2.9), and asks about the person of steady wisdom (2.54), about understanding versus action (3.1–2) and about what drives one to sin (3.36).

name: Sañjaya
summary: The narrator of the Gītā's frame, reporting the scene on the battlefield to Dhṛtarāṣṭra in answer to his question (1.2 onward; 1.24, 1.47, 2.1, 2.9–10).

name: Dhṛtarāṣṭra
summary: The king whose question to Sañjaya opens the text: what did my people and the sons of Pāṇḍu do at Kurukṣetra, the field of dharma? (1.1); addressed by Sañjaya as 'lord of the earth' and 'Bhārata'.

name: Duryodhana
summary: King, son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who goes to his teacher Droṇa, lists the warriors of both armies and orders that Bhīṣma be guarded (1.2–11); called 'the evil-minded son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra' by Arjuna (1.23).

name: Droṇa
summary: The teacher (ācārya) to whom Duryodhana speaks (1.2–11), whose disciple (Dhṛṣṭadyumna) arrayed the opposing army (1.3); named with Bhīṣma as one Arjuna cannot fight, being worthy of worship (1.25, 2.4).

name: Bhīṣma
summary: Protector of the Kaurava army (1.10–11), who blows his conch with a lion's roar (1.12); named with Droṇa as one worthy of worship whom Arjuna cannot fight (1.25, 2.4).

name: Dhṛṣṭadyumna
summary: Son of Drupada and Droṇa's disciple, who arrayed the Pāṇḍava army (1.3); blows his conch (1.17).

name: Bhīma
summary: Pāṇḍava warrior by whom the warriors are measured (1.4), protector of the Pāṇḍava force (1.10), who blows the great conch Pauṇḍra (1.15).

name: Sātyaki
summary: Pāṇḍava warrior named Yuyudhāna in 1.4 and Sātyaki, 'the unconquered', in 1.17 (the two names denote one warrior in the epic).

name: Virāṭa
summary: Pāṇḍava warrior named in Duryodhana's list (1.4) and among the conch-blowers (1.17).

name: Drupada
summary: Great chariot-warrior of the Pāṇḍava army (1.4), father of Dhṛṣṭadyumna (1.3), who blows his conch (1.18).

name: Dhṛṣṭaketu
summary: Pāṇḍava warrior named in Duryodhana's list (1.5).

name: Cekitāna
summary: Pāṇḍava warrior named in Duryodhana's list (1.5).

name: the king of Kāśī
summary: Valiant Pāṇḍava ally named as kāśirāja in Duryodhana's list (1.5) and as kāśya, 'supreme archer', among the conch-blowers (1.17); taken as the same person.

name: Purujit
summary: Pāṇḍava warrior named in Duryodhana's list (1.5).

name: Kuntibhoja
summary: Pāṇḍava warrior named in Duryodhana's list (1.5).

name: Śaibya
summary: Pāṇḍava warrior, 'a bull among men', named in Duryodhana's list (1.5).

name: Yudhāmanyu
summary: Valorous Pāṇḍava warrior named in Duryodhana's list (1.6).

name: Uttamaujas
summary: Valiant Pāṇḍava warrior named in Duryodhana's list (1.6).

name: Abhimanyu
summary: Named in the Gītā only as Saubhadra, the strong-armed son of Subhadrā, a great chariot-warrior who blows his conch (1.6, 1.18); identified as Abhimanyu, Arjuna's son, from the epic.

name: the Draupadeyas (sons of Draupadī)
summary: The sons of Draupadī, named as a group among the great chariot-warriors of the Pāṇḍava army (1.6) and the conch-blowers (1.18). Group entry.

name: Karṇa
summary: Leader of Duryodhana's army named in his list (1.8).

name: Kṛpa
summary: Leader of Duryodhana's army, 'victorious in battle', named in his list (1.8).

name: Aśvatthāman
summary: Leader of Duryodhana's army named in his list (1.8).

name: Vikarṇa
summary: Leader of Duryodhana's army named in his list (1.8).

name: Bhūriśravas
summary: Named in the Gītā only as Saumadatti, 'the son of Somadatta', among the leaders of Duryodhana's army (1.8); usually identified as Bhūriśravas.

name: Yudhiṣṭhira
summary: King, son of Kuntī, who blows the conch Anantavijaya (1.16).

name: Nakula
summary: Pāṇḍava who blows the conch Sughoṣa (1.16).

name: Sahadeva
summary: Pāṇḍava who blows the conch Maṇipuṣpaka (1.16).

name: Śikhaṇḍin
summary: Great chariot-warrior of the Pāṇḍava side who blows his conch (1.17). (The epic's account of Śikhaṇḍin's sex change is not in these verses; gender left 'unknown'.)

name: Pāṇḍu
summary: Named in chapters 1–3 only through his sons, the Pāṇḍavas / sons of Pāṇḍu (1.1, 1.3).

name: Kuntī
summary: Named in chapters 1–3 only through her sons: Yudhiṣṭhira as kuntīputra (1.16) and Arjuna as Kaunteya (1.27 and passim) and Pārtha (son of Pṛthā).

name: Subhadrā
summary: Named in chapters 1–3 only through her son, Saubhadra (1.6, 1.18).

name: Draupadī
summary: Named in chapters 1–3 only through her sons, the Draupadeyas (1.6, 1.18).

name: Somadatta
summary: Named in chapters 1–3 only through his son, Saumadatti (1.8).

name: Prajāpati
summary: The lord of creatures who in the beginning created beings together with sacrifice and told them to prosper by it, to nourish the gods and be nourished by them (3.10–12; quoted by Kṛṣṇa).

name: Janaka
summary: Cited by Kṛṣṇa as precedent: Janaka and others reached perfection (saṃsiddhi) by action alone (3.20).
